You plan days of errands in San Francisco for people without a car. They travel by Muni (buses, Muni Metro, cable cars), BART, and on foot.

Choose one specific store for each errand and the order to visit them so the person finishes everything as early as possible. Respect store opening hours, the time each errand takes, any deadlines, and when they must reach their final destination. If the errands cannot all be done under those constraints, say so.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"feasible": true, "stops": [{"category": "<errand category>", "store_name": "<name>", "address": "<street address>", "poi_id": "<the store's id if ids were given, else null>"}], "reason": null}

- One stop per errand, in visiting order. Use exactly these category names: "bank_atm" (bank or ATM), "bakery" (bakery), "bike_shop" (bike shop), "library" (library), "hardware" (hardware store), "florist" (florist).
- Give each store's name and its street address in San Francisco.
- If it is impossible, reply {"feasible": false, "stops": [], "reason": "<why>"}.

It's Sunday, October 11, and I'm heading out from Union Square (Powell & Geary) (Downtown) around 8:30 am. No car today: just Muni, BART and walking. Today I need to buy flowers at a florist (about 10 minutes), buy picture hooks at a hardware store (about 10 minutes), pick up a loaf of bread at a bakery (about 5 minutes), buy a new inner tube at a bike shop (about 20 minutes), drop off library books at a library (about 10 minutes), and withdraw cash at a bank or ATM (about 5 minutes). I have to pick up a loaf of bread at a bakery by 12:35 pm at the latest. When I'm done I'm meeting a friend at 45th Ave & Judah (Sunset) and need to be there by 1:20 pm. Which specific stores should I go to, and in what order, so I'm done as early as possible? If it can't all be done, tell me it's impossible and why.
